study.name: DEV-2026-VALVE-RCT
study.label: TAVR versus SAVR randomised trial
study.description: Fictional randomised device trial comparing the Vascular Dynamics TAVR System with surgical aortic valve replacement, analysed by win ratio over a hierarchical composite at 1 year. Synthetic reference study; not a real protocol.

versions.rationale: A single-arm investigation shows early safety against a performance goal but cannot compare TAVR with surgery. This randomised trial compares the two on what matters to patients, in order of importance: survival, freedom from disabling stroke, freedom from rehospitalisation, and quality of life.

titles.text: Randomised Clinical Investigation of the Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) System versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis (ISO 14155 / FDA 21 CFR 812)

studyInterventions.name: Vascular Dynamics TAVR System
studyInterventions.description: Self-expanding bioprosthetic aortic valve with a transfemoral delivery catheter.

studyInterventions.name: Surgical aortic valve replacement
studyInterventions.description: Surgical implantation of a commercially available bioprosthetic aortic valve chosen by the site's surgeon, through sternotomy or mini-sternotomy on cardiopulmonary bypass.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Severe aortic stenosis
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Severe aortic stenosis: aortic valve area of 1.0 cm2 or less, or a mean gradient of 40 mmHg or more, on echocardiography.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Symptoms
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: NYHA functional class II or higher.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Suitable for both treatments
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: The heart team, including a cardiac surgeon and an interventional cardiologist, agrees the participant is suitable for both transfemoral TAVR and SAVR.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Bicuspid valve
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Congenital bicuspid or unicuspid aortic valve.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Recent stroke
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Stroke or transient ischaemic attack within 6 months before the index procedure.

studyDesigns.name: Pivotal IDE Clinical Investigation of the Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) System in Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis (ISO 14155 / FDA 21 CFR 812)
studyDesigns.description: Two-arm parallel randomised design. Participants are randomised 1:1 to TAVR or SAVR in permuted blocks, stratified by surgical risk (STS-PROM below 4%, or 4% or above).

activities.name: Subject Demographics & IDE Consent
activities.description: Subject baseline characteristics, demographics, and consent tracking

activities.name: Medical Device Identification & UDI Traceability
activities.description: ISO 14155 / FDA 21 CFR 812 medical device identification, model, lot, and Unique Device Identifier (UDI) tracking

activities.name: Procedural Implantation & Device In-Use
activities.description: Intra-procedural delivery, anatomical site access, deployment outcome, and fluoroscopy duration

activities.name: Device Deficiencies & Adverse Incidents Log
activities.description: Continuous log for ISO 14155 / FDA 21 CFR 812 device malfunctions, use errors, and serious adverse incidents

activities.name: Hemodynamics & Vital Signs Assessment
activities.description: Sitting blood pressure, pulse, temperature, height, weight, and automated BMI

activities.name: Concomitant Antiplatelet / Anticoagulant Therapy
activities.description: Log of prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and supplements

activities.name: Adverse Events & Serious Complications Log
activities.description: Continuous log form for capturing adverse events, CTCAE grading, seriousness, and attribution

activities.name: Clinical events committee adjudication
activities.description: Independent adjudication of each suspected death, stroke, rehospitalisation and VARC-3 event against source documents, blinded to arm.

activities.name: Randomisation
activities.description: Stratified 1:1 randomisation to TAVR or SAVR after eligibility is confirmed.

activities.name: Valve Symptom and Function Score
activities.description: Fictional 0-100 patient-reported questionnaire on symptoms, physical limitation and quality of life (QSCAT VSFS, overall summary QSTESTCD VSFSOS).

arms.name: TAVR System
arms.description: Transfemoral implantation of the investigational transcatheter aortic valve

arms.name: Surgical AVR
arms.description: Surgical replacement of the aortic valve with a commercially available bioprosthesis

studyDesigns.rationale: Randomisation removes the selection that confounds registry comparisons of TAVR and surgery; stratifying by surgical risk balances the strongest prognostic factor between arms.

epochs.name: Screening Epoch
epochs.description: Heart team evaluation, imaging and eligibility

epochs.name: Index Procedure Epoch
epochs.description: Index procedure: TAVR or SAVR as randomised

estimands.name: Primary estimand
estimands.description: TAVR compared with SAVR on the 1-year hierarchical composite in all randomised participants, as randomised.
estimands.populationSummary: Win ratio of TAVR over SAVR: wins divided by losses over all TAVR-SAVR pairs within each surgical-risk stratum, combined with Mantel-Haenszel-type weights, with a two-sided 95% confidence interval and a stratified Finkelstein-Schoenfeld test at two-sided alpha 0.05. Net benefit and win odds are reported alongside.

intercurrentEvents.name: Death
intercurrentEvents.text: Death from any cause before 1 year.

intercurrentEvents.name: Treatment other than randomised
intercurrentEvents.text: The participant receives the other arm's treatment, no valve, or a valve reintervention before 1 year.

intercurrentEvents.name: Withdrawal or loss to follow-up
intercurrentEvents.text: The participant withdraws or is lost to follow-up before 1 year; event levels are compared over the shared follow-up, assuming censoring unrelated to outcome, with an inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted sensitivity analysis.

objectives.name: Primary objective
objectives.text: To compare TAVR with SAVR on a hierarchy of death, disabling stroke, rehospitalisation and quality of life over 1 year.

endpoints.name: Hierarchical composite at 1 year
endpoints.text: Hierarchical composite over 1 year, compared between every TAVR and every SAVR participant within a surgical-risk stratum, decided at the first level that separates the pair: (1) all-cause death, later is better; (2) disabling stroke, later is better; (3) first valve-related or heart-failure rehospitalisation, later is better; (4) change from baseline in the Valve Symptom and Function Score overall summary at 1 year, higher is better, a difference of less than 5 points counting as a tie. Event levels are compared over the follow-up both participants share; a pair missing the 1-year score for either participant is tied at level 4. Events are adjudicated by the clinical events committee.

objectives.name: Component objective
objectives.text: To describe each level of the hierarchy on its own, in hierarchy order.

endpoints.name: All-cause death to 1 year
endpoints.text: Time from randomisation to death from any cause, censored at 365 days.

endpoints.name: Disabling stroke to 1 year
endpoints.text: Time from randomisation to the first adjudicated disabling stroke (modified Rankin Scale 2 or more at 90 days, with an increase of at least 1 from baseline), censored at 365 days.

endpoints.name: Valve-related or heart-failure rehospitalisation to 1 year
endpoints.text: Time from randomisation to the first adjudicated rehospitalisation for valve-related symptoms or worsening heart failure, censored at 365 days.

endpoints.name: Change in Valve Symptom and Function Score at 1 year
endpoints.text: Change from baseline to 1 year in the Valve Symptom and Function Score overall summary (0 to 100, higher is better). The score is a fictional instrument scored like published heart-failure questionnaires; this synthetic study does not use a licensed instrument.

objectives.name: Early safety objective
objectives.text: To compare early safety of TAVR and SAVR.

endpoints.name: VARC-3 early safety composite at 30 days
endpoints.text: VARC-3 early safety composite at 30 days: all-cause death, any stroke, VARC type 2 to 4 bleeding, major vascular, access-related or cardiac structural complication, acute kidney injury stage 3 or 4, moderate or severe aortic regurgitation, new permanent pacemaker due to procedure-related conduction disturbance, or surgery or intervention related to the device. Events are adjudicated by the clinical events committee.

objectives.name: Valve performance objective
objectives.text: To compare the haemodynamic performance of the two valves over one year.

endpoints.name: Mean gradient and valve area at 1 year
endpoints.text: Mean transvalvular gradient and effective orifice area on echocardiography at 1 year.

population.name: Study population
population.description: Adults aged 65 to 85 with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis whom the heart team considers suitable for both transfemoral TAVR and surgical valve replacement.
